finding.claim: GraphQL WebSocket handshakes (asgi, aiohttp, litestar, channels) never validate the Origin header. With cookie-based auth in get_context/on_ws_connect, a cross-site page can open a graphql-transport-ws connection carrying the victim's cookies and run queries and mutations as the victim (cross-site WebSocket hijacking). Conditional on the app authenticating via cookies and cookies being sent cross-site.
finding.source: Cross-site attacker page opens WebSocket to the victim's GraphQL endpoint; browser attaches the victim's cookies to the handshake.
finding.sink: schema.stream(...) executing queries and mutations under the victim's session (default allowed operation types include MUTATION).

trace.note: get_context built from handshake request before accept, no origin check
create_websocket_response calls accept() with no Origin check
handle_connection_init; on_ws_connect defaults to UNSET so no auth by default
stream falls back to DEFAULT_ALLOWED_OPERATION_TYPES (schema.py:122-126), which includes MUTATION

finding.guards_checked: Searched all of strawberry/ (excluding codemods) for origin, Origin, Sec-WebSocket, check_origin, allowed_origins: no Origin validation in any HTTP or WS integration (only get_origin type helpers matched). connection_acknowledged only enforces connection_init happened; it does not authenticate. Legacy graphql-ws path uses schema.subscribe restricted to SUBSCRIPTION (schema.py:1240), so not exposed to mutations. Exploitability depends on app cookie auth and SameSite attributes.

finding.claim: When multipart_uploads_enabled is True, a cross-site form POST with multipart/form-data is accepted and can execute mutations under cookie-based session auth, with no CSRF token or custom-header requirement. Opt-in: multipart is disabled by default.
finding.source: Cross-site HTML form POST with Content-Type multipart/form-data from attacker origin; browser sends victim cookies if SameSite permits.
finding.sink: execute_single -> schema.execute running a mutation (POST allows MUTATION).

trace.note: parse_http_body: non-GET dispatch by content type
parse_multipart reads operations/map/files from form, no CSRF check
execute_single builds allowed types from request method

finding.guards_checked: Multipart disabled by default (strawberry/http/base.py:35). GET cannot run mutations (types/graphql.py:17-22; async_base_view.py:198-199). JSON path requires application/json (async_base_view.py:582-583), which triggers CORS preflight and is not CSRF-able. text/plain rejected (async_base_view.py:587). No token or custom-header requirement exists for multipart. Exploitability depends on app enabling multipart and cookie SameSite attributes.
